title: The Second Book of the Kings, with Introduction and Notes (Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges)

verification_log.method: On 22:8: the law had been neglected for nearly sixty years under Manasseh and Amon, so its loss is unsurprising; on 22:20 "in peace": none of the denounced evils would come in his time; on 23:29: Necho's "expedition against the king of Assyria was B.C. 610"; Necho probably came by sea; "Josiah at this time was in alliance with, or perhaps tributary to, Assyria"; on 23:30: from Zech 12:11 it "has been supposed that Josiah did not die till he reached Hadad-Rimmon"; Jeremiah's dirge probably lost; on 23:22–23: Kings omits Hezekiah's passover; the point is that none had been kept in this complete form since Samuel
